true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate self.downsize definition silently overrides 4-arg version

Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145-147 with `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and lines 149-151 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`). In Ruby the second definition replaces the first, so any existing caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` will now pass `height` as the `opts` hash position and raise ArgumentError or build wrong instructions. Use a single method with an optional/flexible signature.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb settings

`maxSizeKB` was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, discarding the per-type site settings. Attachments (which are not downsized server-side) can now be submitted far above the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` and will be rejected only by the server, and admins who lowered/raised the limits get an inconsistent client-side check and a misleading error message. The same hardcoding at line 246 shows the wrong size in the 413 message.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsize loop can spin without shrinking and ignores failures

The loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%")` while `tempfile.size` exceeds the limit. `tempfile.size` on an already-opened Tempfile may be cached/stale after the external `convert` rewrites the file on disk (the Ruby File object's size is read via fstat, but the file position/content is replaced out of band), so the check may not reflect the new size. Also the return value of `downsize` is ignored: if `convert` fails, the loop still runs 5 times and the oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for`, producing no useful error. Should check the return value and break on failure, and re-stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL download size cap hardcoded to 10MB

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` no longer respects `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so API-provided URLs can always pull up to 10MB regardless of site configuration; for non-image files there is no downsizing fallback, so the admin-configured limit is effectively bypassed at download time.

Downsizing in-place with same source and destination path

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same file as ImageMagick input and output. Converting in place is unreliable (and gifsicle's `--output` to the same file as input is explicitly unsafe), risking a truncated/corrupt upload. Write to a new temp file and swap.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises on nil host instead of failing validation

`self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. Creating/saving an `EmbeddableHost` with a nil host (e.g. an admin submitting a blank host — the controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly) raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing/deleted record; `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` on nil, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`).

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host lookup is not case-insensitive on the input side

`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value derived from the referer/URL. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `uri.host == "EvilTrout.com"`, which never matches the lowercased column, so legitimate embeds are rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Pass `host.downcase`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped host value interpolated into INSERT statement

The host string comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting and is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A host containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) breaks the statement or allows SQL injection during migration. Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized insert. Additionally the raw value is not stripped of `http://`/paths like `EmbeddableHost`'s before_validation does, so migrated rows will not match `record_for_host` lookups and embedding will silently break after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents swapped between category and embeddable_host files

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file names no longer describe their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for `Fabricate(:category)` or `Fabricate(:private_category)`. Swap the contents.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped host value interpolated into INSERT statement

The host string comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting and is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A host containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) breaks the statement or allows SQL injection during migration. Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized insert. Additionally the raw value is not stripped of `http://`/paths like `EmbeddableHost`'s before_validation does, so migrated rows will not match `record_for_host` lookups and embedding will silently break after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when no category matches embed_category

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row is returned. On the overwhelming majority of sites the `embed_category` site setting row does not exist (it is never saved unless changed), so the result set is empty and `[0]` is `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`. Every such site fails to migrate. Use a nil-safe fetch (e.g. `rows.first && rows.first['id'].to_i`) before falling back to uncategorized.

false_positives.candidate:
Embedding#update is a no-op

`update` performs no state change but returns 200 with the serialized embedding, and the client's `saveChanges` calls `embedding.update({})`. Any future/implied 'save settings' action on this page silently does nothing, which is misleading to callers. Either implement the update or drop the route and the client action.

No request specs for the new embeddable hosts endpoints

The only assertion is that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. The new create/update/destroy actions (including the nil-record paths and the uncategorized-category fallback) and the embedding show/update endpoints are untested, so regressions such as the 500 on a missing id would not be caught.

No uniqueness constraint or index on host

Nothing prevents two `embeddable_hosts` rows with the same host (the model has no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index). `record_for_host` then silently picks an arbitrary row, making the category used for embedded topics nondeterministic. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on `lower(host)`.

Plural embedded hydration assumes array and keeps undefined entries

`obj[k].map(...)` is called without checking that `obj[k]` is an array; any attribute whose name matches `(.+)_ids$` but holds null/a scalar throws a TypeError during hydration. Additionally, unlike the singular branch, the plural branch deletes the original `_ids` key unconditionally and stores entries that may be `undefined` when a sub-object is not sideloaded, silently producing a collection of undefined models (which is exactly what happens with the embedding payload).

PostCreator `category:` option now receives an id instead of a name

The previous code passed `category: SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name string; the new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer. If PostCreator's `category` option is resolved by name, the embedded topic will land in no/uncategorized category instead of the configured one. Verify PostCreator's contract and pass `category_id` (or the name) accordingly — the added spec only asserts equality when the fabricated host's category happens to resolve.

create_table force: true in migration can drop an existing table

`create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS first. If the migration is re-run or the table already exists for any reason, existing embeddable host rows are destroyed without warning. Also, because the migration uses `execute` inside `change` (including a destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings`), it is not reversible; it should be split into `up`/`down`.

has_many with embed: :ids does not include the host objects, admin page will show no hosts

`has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` serializes only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not sideload the actual `embeddable_hosts` array. The Ember store's `_hydrateEmbedded` looks up the ids in `root['embeddable_hosts']`, which is absent, so hydration yields `undefined` entries and the embedding admin template renders empty/broken rows. Use `embed: :ids, include: true` (or sideload the collection explicitly).

replace('_','-') only converts the first underscore

`type.replace('_', '-')` without the `g` flag replaces only the first underscore, so a future admin model type with two or more underscores (e.g. `site_customization_thing`) would not match an entry in ADMIN_MODELS and would be requested from the non-admin path. Use `.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser record exists

`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user can receive a notification email for a topic without a topic_users row, e.g. mailing-list mode or a record cleaned up), and `notification_level` can also be NULL. The subsequent `tu.notification_level > ...` then raises NoMethodError on nil, giving a 500 to anyone following the unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` or create the record if missing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText

The computed property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` ('Notificiations') here and in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs. While consistent today, the typo is part of the public controller API and will break silently if anyone fixes one side; rename both to `stopNotificationsText`.

false_positives.candidate:
No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint

The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (auth requirement, slug redirect, nil TopicUser, level toggling) and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` have no request/model specs. Given the nil-dereference and toggle semantics above, these paths are untested and regressions will ship silently.

Repeat visits to unsubscribe URL mute the topic unexpectedly

The toggle logic lowers watching/tracking to :regular on the first visit, but any subsequent hit of the same URL (back button, re-opening the email, prefetch) falls into the else branch and sets :muted. Combined with the email text/UI claiming 'You will stop receiving notifications', the resulting state is non-deterministic from the user's point of view. Make the endpoint idempotent (always target one level) or require an explicit confirmation action.

State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET

`unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level on a plain GET request (routes.rb line 440/441) with `check_xhr` skipped and no token. Email clients, link prefetchers, antivirus scanners and third-party sites embedding the URL can silently mute topics for the user (CSRF-by-GET). The link should land on a confirmation page and perform the change via a POST/PUT with a signed key, as the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow does.

topicUnsubscribe route shadowed by topic fromParamsNear

The `topic` resource declared above defines `fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost` under `/t/:slug/:id`, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` is matched first with nearPost='unsubscribe' and never reaches the new `topicUnsubscribe` route. The unsubscribe page will not render client-side (and the post stream request with a non-numeric nearPost will fail). The new route must be declared before the topic resource or nested with a numeric constraint.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url and will raise for other callers

server.en.yml's `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `unsubscribe_url` is only supplied by `UserNotifications#send_notification_email`. Any other build_email call that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will make `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in both `body` and `html_part`, breaking those emails. Either default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` or guard the interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
match_count update uses non-atomic save and ignores failures

`record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads-modifies-writes outside a transaction, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose counts, and a failed `save` (e.g. validation) is silently swallowed while the block decision still proceeds. Prefer an atomic `update_all`/`increment!`-style SQL update.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive and not normalized

`should_block?` does an exact `where(email: email)` match. Emails in the users table are stored/compared downcased elsewhere (see `Email.downcase` usage), but blocked entries are stored verbatim from the migration/fabricator with no normalization callback. A blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` is trivially bypassed by signing up as `Bad@Spam.com`. Downcase/strip the email both before persisting a BlockedEmail and in the lookup.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
No specs cover whitelist/blacklist behaviour after move out of User

The domain whitelist/blacklist logic was removed from `User#email_validator` and moved here, but the new spec only stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`. If the existing user specs referenced the removed private methods they would break, and either way the whitelist/blacklist branches of the new validator are untested, so a regression in the regex construction would go unnoticed.

Signup failure response now echoes full error hash and submitted values

The create response now includes `user.errors.to_hash` and the submitted name/username/email. This makes account enumeration easier programmatically (e.g. distinguishing "email already taken" from other failures) and reflects user input back into JSON. If only the email rejection flag is needed by the client, return a minimal, specific field instead of the whole error hash.

rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances

Declaring `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` directly on the class body puts a single array on the prototype, shared by every instance of CreateAccountController (and never reset when the modal is reopened). Because the code mutates it with `pushObject`, emails rejected in one session stay rejected forever for the page lifetime, and any other instance sees them too. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in `init`, `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`) and clear it when the modal is shown.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Weak postMessage origin check using substring match

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL (e.g. `http://disc` prefixes, or `https://x` if present inside the URL), and conversely rejects nothing reliably. Compare the event origin for exact equality with the Discourse origin instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB/Ruby `<%- end if %>` breaks the view

Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>`. `end if` with a bare `if` modifier and no condition is a Ruby syntax error, so rendering embed/best will raise instead of producing the page. It should simply be `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
poll_feed assumes every feed item has `content`

`i.content.scrub` will raise NoMethodError on nil for RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `description` (SimpleRSS only populates `content`/`content_encoded` for Atom-style feeds). Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such feed permanently breaks polling. Fall back to `i.description`/`content_encoded` and skip blank items.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)

`parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no escaping. EmbedController#ensure_embeddable only validates the referer's *host*, so an attacker on the embeddable host (or anyone who can set an arbitrary Referer, e.g. a crafted request) can supply a referer like `http://host/x');alert(1);//` and execute arbitrary script in the context of the Discourse origin. Escape with `j`/`to_json` or build the target origin from scheme+host only.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

false_positives.candidate:
content_sha1 updated even when revise! fails

`revisor.revise!` can return false (e.g. `should_revise?` false) or `@post.save` can fail validation silently, yet `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. The embed then records the new checksum while the post still holds the old content, so the update will never be retried on subsequent imports. Only update the sha when the revision actually succeeded.

create_table with force: true in migrations can drop existing tables

`create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (and the same change made to 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If the table already exists on an installation, running the migration silently destroys its data. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

import mutates the caller's contents string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller. Callers that reuse or cache the string (e.g. retrying the import, or passing a frozen/literal string) will see the footer appended repeatedly, or get a RuntimeError on a frozen string. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML, enabling XSS from feeds

`cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the sanitizing render pipeline. TopicEmbed.import (used by Jobs::PollFeed on arbitrary RSS/ATOM content) passes feed HTML straight through with this cook method, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Any `<script>`/event-handler markup in a polled feed (or any content the feed author controls) becomes executable script on the forum. The HTML should be sanitized/whitelisted before being stored as cooked.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
.d-header .contents previously relied on floats for layout; floated non-flex descendants may need review

Converting .contents to flex removes the effect of float on its direct children (the old `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted). `.icons`/`.login-button` still use `float: left` but are inside .panel, which is not a flex container, so they still work; however there is no `flex-wrap`/`min-width: 0` on the flex items, so long titles can overflow instead of shrinking as they did with the float layout. Worth verifying narrow-viewport header rendering.

align-items mixin emits invalid values for legacy prefixes

The mixin blindly forwards the argument to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept start/end/center/baseline/stretch. Calling `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` (likely in future use) emits invalid declarations for those legacy properties, silently losing alignment in old WebKit/IE10. Either map values or drop the obsolete box-model prefixes.

float: right on a flex item is ignored after making .small-action a flex container

.small-action is now `display: flex` (line 264), so `float` on its direct children has no effect. The `button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) and `clear: both` (line 312) are now dead, meaning the small-action action button will no longer be pushed to the right edge but will sit immediately after the description. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button instead (as was done for .d-header .panel).

order(3) on .panel without explicit order on siblings relies on default order 0

.d-header .panel gets `@include order(3)` while .title has no order and .extra-info-wrapper (topic.scss) gets order(2). For the legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` prefix the initial value is 1, not 0, so under old WebKit the un-ordered .title (group 1) and the explicitly ordered items still work, but any sibling relying on default ordering is fragile; also `order(3)` is redundant given `margin-left: auto` already pushes .panel right. Consider setting explicit orders on all header flex children or dropping the order include.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the trailing `?` so it never gates serialization

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always included in the payload, even when the website is blank (serialized as `null`). Rename to `include_website_name?`.

false_positives.candidate:
Host comparison is case-sensitive and parses the URI repeatedly

`website_host` and `Discourse.current_hostname` are compared with `==`/`ends_with?` without downcasing. A profile URL such as `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` yields host `EXAMPLE.com` which will not match hostname `example.com`, so the full-path behaviour this PR adds silently fails. Downcase both hosts before comparing. (`URI(website.to_s)` is also built three times; parse once.)

No test for sibling-subdomain and blank-website cases

The new specs cover only equal host, different host, and parent-domain host. Missing: website blank/invalid (verifying `website_name` is omitted, which currently fails because `include_website_name?` is misnamed), and the sibling subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance) which is the most fragile piece of the new logic.

Subdomain match only works when label counts are equal

The second branch requires `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and >2 labels, so cases like website `www.example.com` with instance `forum.eu.example.com`, or website `example.co.uk` with instance `forum.example.co.uk` (handled only by the `ends_with?` branch, which works) are inconsistent: sibling subdomains with different depths fall back to host-only. Consider comparing registrable suffixes instead of label counts.

Use `+` instead of `<<` for string concatenation here

`"." << website_host` mutates the receiver string in place; while the literal is a fresh object today, this breaks if `# frozen_string_literal: true` is ever added to the file and is needlessly surprising. Use `"." + website_host`.

website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 website to anonymous users

`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user seen by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, so the website host (and now possibly the full path) is still exposed for TL0 users to anonymous visitors, defeating the existing spam-prevention restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and extend the TL0 spec's `untrusted_attributes` list accordingly.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

Offset clamped to user_count yields an empty last page

`offset = Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))` allows offset == user_count, which requests a range past the last member and returns zero members. The upper clamp should be `Math.max(user_count - limit, 0)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
remove_member test uses PUT while the route only accepts DELETE, and relies on hardcoded group id 1

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but config/routes.rb maps only `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages off-by-one for exact multiples of limit

`totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With user_count=50 and limit=50 this yields 2 pages, the second of which is empty; the 'next' arrow stays enabled and `showingLast` never matches on the real last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Unbounded `limit` param on public members endpoint

`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is not capped, and this endpoint is public (only subject to group visibility). A caller can pass `limit=1000000` and force serialization of every group member, a cheap way to generate heavy DB/CPU load. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 50–200) and reject negative values.

`{{each}}` used with block-param syntax but no closing tag

`{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` mixes the keyword (`x in y`) form, which requires a block and `{{/each}}`, with the inline `itemView` form. As written the template will either fail to compile or render nothing, so the member list never appears on the admin group page.

addMembers/removeMember failures are silently swallowed

`addMembers` and `removeMember` call into the model without attaching a rejection handler, so a server error (e.g. 422 for an automatic group, or an unknown username) produces no user feedback and the input is never cleared (per the TODO). Add an error handler that surfaces the response errors via bootbox like `save` does.

group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer to an AR collection

`remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an Integer. ActiveRecord collection `delete` expects record objects (or at least responds unpredictably to raw ids, raising NoMethodError on `id`/`destroyed?` in many versions). The member will not be removed, or the request will 500. It should look up the user (`user = User.find_by(id: user_id)`) and call `group.remove(user)` / `group.users.delete(user)`, and return a 404/422 if the user isn't found.

update silently clears `visible` and never persists alias_level on create

In `update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally, so any PUT that omits `visible` (e.g. a partial update from a future client or an API caller) flips the group to not-visible. Additionally `create` only reads `name` and `visible`, so the `alias_level` the client sends in `asJSON()` on group creation is dropped, and new groups always get the default alias level. Use `params.key?(:visible)` guards and handle `alias_level` in `create`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
ensure_loaded!/@loaded_locales initialization is not thread-safe

`I18n.ensure_loaded!` reads and lazily initializes `@loaded_locales` outside `LOAD_MUTEX` (only `load_locale` takes the lock). Under concurrent requests on a threaded server, two threads can simultaneously see nil/stale arrays and `@loaded_locales << locale` from different threads can lose entries, causing redundant loads or a locale being considered loaded while its translations are only partially installed. Perform the check and initialization under the same mutex.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales only loaded in web requests; jobs/mailers get missing translations

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because `translate` lazily loads only `config.locale`, any code path outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console, console-driven digests) performing a lookup in a locale with a missing key will have the fallback locale's YAML not loaded, so the Fallbacks backend finds nothing and raises/returns a missing-translation instead of the fallback string. The loading should be hooked into the lookup path (e.g. inside `translate`/`load_locale`) or into the job/mailer locale setup as well.

No tests for fallback behaviour

This PR introduces a new fallback chain (user locale -> site default locale -> :en) plus lazy loading of fallback locale files, but adds no specs. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in the user locale resolves from the site default locale and then from English, nor that fallback locale YAML is actually loaded before lookup. Given the silent-failure mode (missing translation strings shown to users), a spec for FallbackLocaleList#[] and an end-to-end translation fallback spec should be added.

SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym can raise NoMethodError

`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` calls `to_sym` on the setting value before any nil check. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil or blank (e.g. during early boot, before site settings are provisioned, or in a DB-less/migration context), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil`. Since this method is invoked on every I18n fallback lookup and from `ensure_loaded!` in a before_filter, a single nil setting breaks all translation. The trailing `.compact` cannot help because the exception happens while building the array; guard with `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` instead.

Translation LRU cache key ignores fallback locales

The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new Fallbacks backend, the resolved value for a given key/locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of FallbackLocaleList). After an admin changes the site default locale, previously cached entries resolved through the old fallback remain in the LRU cache and are served, producing stale/incorrect translations until a process restart or `I18n.reload!`. The fallback chain (or default_locale) should be part of the cache key, or the cache must be invalidated when default_locale changes.

translate can NoMethodError on nil @loaded_locales

`translate` does `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` without initializing `@loaded_locales`, while the newly added `ensure_loaded!` defensively does `@loaded_locales ||= []`. If any translation happens before `reload!` has run (the only place that initializes the ivar), `translate` raises `NoMethodError` on nil. Initialize the ivar consistently (e.g. `@loaded_locales ||= []` in `translate` too) rather than relying on call ordering.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()

Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires non-null user, disabling passkeys on the initial login form

`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. In `authenticate()` the webauthn form data is now filled only if this returns true, so for a normal (non re-authentication) login where `context.getUser() == null`, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked and the conditional-UI/passkeys attributes are absent from the login page. true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative slice start raises ValueError in Django QuerySet

In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (the comment claiming the ORM handles it is false). Any request with a negative cursor offset against this endpoint will produce an unhandled 500. The same applies in `BasePaginator.get_result` line 182 where negative offsets are still passed through when `cursor.is_prev` is true.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError

`organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for requests that are not made by an organization member (e.g. token/sentry-app auth or a staff user outside the org), so this will raise `AttributeError` and return a 500 on an endpoint that previously worked. Guard with `organization_context.member and ...`.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime keys

`get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. Likewise `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value, which is then compared against a datetime column in `build_queryset`, producing invalid SQL/incorrect filtering. Requests with `optimized_pagination=true` will fail or return wrong pages; a DateTime-aware key implementation (like `DateTimePaginator`) is required.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Client-controlled query param selects paginator that bypasses offset bounds

`optimized_pagination=true` is a user-supplied query parameter that switches to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which explicitly permits offsets outside normal pagination bounds (negative OFFSET/cursor values). The in-code justification that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is only true for the organization filter; arbitrary offsets are not a permission boundary and expose unvalidated, error-prone query paths to any superuser or member with global access. Either remove the parameter or validate offsets server-side.

Misleading comment about negative offsets in Cursor

The added comment states that negative offsets are allowed as a "performance optimization" enabling reverse pagination, but `Cursor` performs no validation at all and downstream paginators cannot actually use negative offsets (Django queryset slicing rejects them). The comment misdocuments behaviour and encourages callers to construct invalid cursors.

New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests

`OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the new `optimized_pagination` branch of the audit log endpoint are added without any unit or API tests. The datetime key bug and negative-offset ValueError would both have been caught by a basic test exercising the new branch.

Offset clamping made inconsistent with later length check

`BasePaginator.get_result` now slices from `start_offset = max(0, offset)` but the subsequent prev-page trimming still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the unclamped `offset`. When `offset` differs from `start_offset` (negative offsets) the trim condition can never match, so the extra fetched row is returned to the client, producing an over-sized page and wrong next/prev cursors. The clamping logic should be applied consistently, or negative offsets rejected as before.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-controlled query param enables negative-offset pagination path

`optimized_pagination=true` plus `enable_advanced_features=True` lets a request opt into `OptimizedCursorPaginator`'s branch that passes an unvalidated, possibly negative `cursor.offset` directly into a queryset slice. Cursor offsets come from the user-supplied `cursor` query param (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative integers and no validation was added). This is an unaudited, user-reachable code path that bypasses the offset sanity checks every other paginator enforces (`BadPaginationError('Pagination offset cannot be negative')`), and the whole feature is unrelated to the stated purpose of this PR (spans buffer). It should be removed or gated behind a real permission check plus validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets for next-page, still passes them through for prev

`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes long-standing behavior: a negative offset is now silently clamped on forward pages (masking bad cursors rather than failing), while negative offsets are still forwarded unchanged when `cursor.is_prev`, where they will hit Django's negative-slice error. Also the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses the raw `offset`, so it no longer matches the actual slice when clamping occurred, which can drop or keep the wrong extra row on prev pages.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime keys used by the audit log endpoint

`get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, which works only for numeric keys. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by='-datetime'`, where the attribute is a `datetime`; `math.floor()` on a datetime raises `TypeError`. Any request hitting the optimized branch will 500. The paginator either needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion or must not be used for datetime ordering.

true_positives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`organization_context.member` may be None -> AttributeError 500

`organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. For a superuser or staff user who is not a member of the organization, `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None`, so this raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500 for every GET of the audit log endpoint, not just when `optimized_pagination` is passed (Python evaluates the right operand of `or` whenever `is_superuser` is False, and `is_superuser` is False for non-superuser members too — in that case `member` is set, but non-member staff/non-member superuser-less tokens will crash). Reorder/short-circuit with `organization_context.member and ...` and only compute it when needed.

false_positives.candidate:
Module docstring still describes Redis sets, not sorted sets

The storage was changed from SET (`sadd`/`sscan`/`sunionstore`) to ZSET (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zunionstore`) with score = `end_timestamp_precise`, but the docstring still says 'Add the ingested span's payload to the set under set_key' and 'span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys'. It also doesn't mention the new per-segment span eviction, which is the key behavioral change of this PR.

No test covers the new span eviction path

The core change of this PR is evicting spans once a segment exceeds the size cap (`zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua), plus the switch to score-ordered storage. No test inserts more than the cap to assert that the oldest-by-`end_timestamp_precise` spans are dropped and the newest retained, nor that `redirect_depth`/`span_count` accounting stays correct when both the span_key and parent_key union branches run. Add a test that exceeds the limit.

Redirect-chain depth limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 without justification

The loop bound was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about segment trees deeper than the limit not being joined correctly was deleted. Traces with redirect chains between 1000 and 10000 that previously merged correctly will now be split into separate segments. If the reduction is intentional (to bound script runtime), keep a comment stating the consequence; otherwise restore the previous bound.

Span eviction limit hardcoded to 1000 and not aligned with max_segment_spans

The new `zpopmin` eviction uses the literal 1000, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` defaults to 1001 and is now unused (the span-count guard was removed from `_load_segment_data`). The cap is no longer configurable and silently drops spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` with no metric/log, so oversized segments lose data invisibly. Pass the limit in as an ARGV from `max_segment_spans` and emit a metric when spans are evicted.

max_segment_spans is now dead configuration

`_load_segment_data` no longer checks `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`, and the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric is gone, yet `max_segment_spans` remains a constructor parameter. Operators setting it get no effect; the enforcement now lives as a hardcoded 1000 in Lua. Either wire the attribute through to the script or remove the parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache key uses Python's randomized hash(), making the cache unstable and collision-prone

The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's `hash()` for tuples of ints is deterministic per-process but string/salted hashing and, more importantly, inter-process agreement is not guaranteed across versions/configurations; worse, collisions on the truncated hash mean two different project sets can share one cache entry and get the wrong upsampling decision. The invalidation helper (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`) computes the key the same way, so a key produced in one worker can be unreachable from another. Use a stable, explicit representation (e.g. sorted ids joined by ",", or a md5/sha of it).

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Column transform duplicated in three branches instead of once

`if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is repeated in the top-events, rpc, and default branches. Besides the duplication, the upsampling decision is computed from the outer `dataset` while the query may actually run against `split_dataset`/`discover` passed in as `scoped_dataset` (see get_event_stats_factory), so an errors-dataset decision can be applied to a discover query and vice versa. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the eligibility check and transform once.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
60s caching of allowlist eligibility silently serves stale upsampling decisions

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by org+project set. Because the result drives whether `count()` is replaced by `sum(sample_weight)`, a stale cache entry means the same query returns counts off by the sample-rate factor (e.g. 10x) for up to a minute after an allowlist change, and users will see charts flip between upsampled and raw values. There is no invalidation hook wired to the option change (the provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in this PR). The option lookup is already an in-memory/cached option read, so the added cache gives little benefit for a real correctness risk; consider dropping it or wiring invalidation to the option update signal.

Accidental git submodule 'sentry-repo' committed

A gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d2909 was added, with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will break `git submodule` operations and clones/CI for anyone checking out the branch. It is unrelated to the feature and should be removed.

Allowlist membership test is O(n*m) on a list

`allowlist` comes from `options.get(...)` as a list and is then used with `project_id in allowlist` for every project. For large allowlists and multi-project queries this is quadratic on a hot API path. Convert to a `set` once before the `all(...)` check.

Bare `except Exception: pass` hides malformed sample-rate data

Both try/except blocks swallow all exceptions silently. A non-numeric or malformed `client_sample_rate` will silently leave `sample_rate` unset, so an upsampling test would fail with a confusing count mismatch rather than the real cause. Narrow to `(TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError)` and/or avoid the try entirely by using `.get()` chains on known dict types.

Naive substring match treats negated error queries as error-focused

`_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query string contains `event.type:error`. Queries like `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, or a message search containing that literal text will be classified as error-only, so `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over rows that include transactions (where `sample_weight` is absent/0), producing wrong counts. Parse the query (or require the dataset to be `errors`) rather than substring matching.

New `upsampled_count` function is publicly exposed in discover

`SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the neighbouring internal functions. That means any API consumer can request `upsampled_count()` on any project, bypassing the allowlist gating in `error_upsampling.py` and getting `sum(sample_weight)` values for non-upsampled projects (where sample_weight may be null/0, producing misleading numbers). Mark it private if it is only meant to be injected by the server-side transform.

No test covers the new caching path; cached values can leak between tests

The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and never call `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, so the newly added cache read/write and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are untested. The endpoint tests in test_organization_events_stats.py mock `options` but do not clear the cache between tests; since the cache key only depends on org id + project ids, an entry written by `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` can make a later test with a different mocked allowlist return the stale eligibility, producing order-dependent flakes.

Test factory derives sample_rate from error_sampling context, diverging from production ingestion

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` injects `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` only inside the test factory. If production relay/event-manager does not do the same, the new snuba tests (asserting count == 10 for a 0.1 sample rate) will pass while the real pipeline never populates `sample_weight`, giving false confidence. The derivation belongs in the real normalization path, or the tests should assert against data produced the production way.

Unused `organization` parameter in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled

`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled(project_ids, organization)` never uses `organization`; the allowlist is purely project-id based. The parameter misleads callers into thinking the check is org-scoped (it isn't, so project ids from other orgs would pass). Either remove it or validate project ownership.

Upsampling eligibility recomputed on every _get_event_stats invocation

`_get_event_stats` is called up to four times per request by the dashboard-split logic, and each call re-runs `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (option read + cache get/set). The comment claims the result is cached for consistency, but nothing is memoized per-request. Compute it once outside the closure (it depends only on snuba_params/organization/dataset/request) to avoid repeated work and guarantee a consistent decision across the split queries.

upsampled_count declares default_result_type "number" while returning Int64

The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64` but `default_result_type` is `"number"` rather than `"integer"` as used by the other count functions. The response meta will advertise a float-ish type for an integer count, which can affect client formatting/axis rendering.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error IDs may be paired with the wrong nodestore payload

`fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. The returned mapping is keyed by node id, and nothing guarantees its iteration order matches the input list (backends may batch/dedupe, and missing entries are filtered out *after* the zip pairing, so one missing/reordered node shifts every subsequent pair). The result is `ErrorEvent.id` values attached to a different event's title/message/timestamp, producing incorrect summaries. Iterate `node_ids` explicitly and look up `events[node_id]` keyed by its corresponding error id.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New table visualization path renders a permanently empty table

When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and hard-coded empty `tableData` (`data: []`, `meta.fields: {}`), completely ignoring the `result`/`fields`/`result.meta` that `StyledSimpleTableChart` receives in the non-flagged branch. Any org with the flag on will see blank table widgets instead of their data. The real result/meta must be mapped into `TabularData`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics recorded before feature/permission gate

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` check, so every rejected (404) request is counted as an assemble event. This inflates the metric with requests that never assemble anything; move the record call after the feature check.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

false_positives.candidate:
Reports with neither `age` nor `timestamp` are accepted

Both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and DRF only runs `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` when the field is present. A report containing neither field therefore validates successfully, even though the spec requires exactly one. Add an object-level `validate()` that rejects the both-absent case so the metric isn't recorded for unusable payloads.

Shared slow-condition map is keyed only by dcg_ids, risking KeyError

`dcg_to_slow_conditions` is now computed once from `event_data.dcg_ids` and passed to both `get_condition_query_groups` and `get_groups_to_fire`. Previously `get_condition_query_groups` built its map from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`. If those two sets ever differ (a DCG present in `dcg_to_groups` but not in `dcg_ids`), `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` raises KeyError and the whole delayed-workflow batch fails. Use a `defaultdict(list)`/`.get(dcg.id, [])` or compute the map from the union of both id sources.

TabularColumn.name typed as the field-key union prevents custom display names

`TabularColumn<TFields>` declares `name: TFields`, the same union as `key`. Since a documented purpose of the prop is "custom display names for columns" (see tableWidgetVisualization docs/stories), arbitrary labels like `'Count of Span Duration'` will not type-check against a constrained `TFields`. `name` should be `string`.

get_environment_info fetches a recommended event per issue

`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for each of the top issues while building a PR comment. This performs a Snuba/nodestore lookup plus an environment query per issue inside a loop in the comment workflow, adding several round trips to every merged-PR comment task and silently swallowing all failures. Consider resolving environments in bulk or reusing data already fetched for the top-issues query.

true_positives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Component exported as `TwoFactor` in BackupCode.tsx

The default export in `BackupCode.tsx` is declared as `function TwoFactor(...)`, which is misleading in React devtools/stack traces and confusing for anyone searching for the backup-code component. Rename to `BackupCode`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
backupCodes state typed as never[] and blob URL leaked on unmount

`useState([])` infers `never[]`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and `backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)` are only accepted because the payload is `any`; this silently defeats type checking. Additionally the object URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked when a new one is created — if the modal unmounts the URL is never revoked, leaking the blob (which contains the plaintext backup codes) for the lifetime of the document. Type the state as `string[]` and revoke the URL in a cleanup effect.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code login unusable for non-CAL identity providers

For users whose identityProvider is GOOGLE/SAML, 2FA is completed via the `/auth/login?totp=...` flow. In that flow the user submits only `backupCode` with an empty `totpCode`, so the earlier guard at line 113 (`user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode`) throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` before the new backup-code branch is reached. SSO users therefore can never use the "Lost access" backup-code path even though the UI offers it.

Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed

Backup codes are persisted as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(codes))` (setup.ts) and compared by decrypting and `indexOf` here. Backup codes are password-equivalent second-factor secrets; storing them in a reversibly encrypted blob means a DB dump plus the (often co-located) CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY yields plaintext second factors for every user. They should be hashed individually (e.g. bcrypt/argon2) and compared by hash, as is done for passwords.

Consumed backup code replaced by null, leaving holes in array

`backupCodes[index] = null` keeps a `null` entry in the stored JSON instead of removing it. Any future code that counts remaining codes, displays them, or validates the array shape must handle nulls; `JSON.parse` of this array also makes `indexOf` semantics depend on nulls never being produced by user input. Filtering the code out (or storing a per-code used flag) would be safer.

JSON.parse / symmetricDecrypt of backupCodes can throw an unhandled error

If `user.backupCodes` was written with a different encryption key or is otherwise corrupt, `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` throws a raw exception that surfaces as a generic 500 rather than a meaningful ErrorCode, breaking login for that user with no diagnostic. Wrap in try/catch and map to `ErrorCode.InternalServerError` (same applies to disable.ts line 58).

No rate limiting or brute-force protection on backup-code verification when disabling 2FA

The login path calls `checkRateLimitAndThrowError` before verifying credentials, but this endpoint verifies an attacker-supplied `backupCode` against the decrypted code list with no rate limit and no invalidation of failed attempts. With a stolen session cookie plus known password this allows unlimited guessing of 10-char hex codes. Add rate limiting consistent with the login flow.

No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code

The new feature's core behavior (authenticating with a backup code, single-use invalidation, rejecting an already-used or wrong code) is untested; only the backup-code display/download/copy UI is exercised. The TODO acknowledges this. Without a test, regressions in the authorize() backup-code branch would silently allow or block logins.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

The recurring-cancellation block (iterating all user calendar credentials × all updatedBookings) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. The rewritten dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which downstream code (org-aware booker URLs / org slug resolution) relies on, so dynamic group bookings for org users may lose organization context. Additionally, the thrown plain `Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is neither `HttpError` nor a Prisma error, so it is converted to a 500 instead of the former 400-style validation failure.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced by the literal string "refresh_token"

When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the code sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers (e.g. zoom, office365) persist the parsed data as the credential key, so a bogus refresh token is written to the DB, silently destroying the real refresh token stored previously and making future refreshes fail with invalid_grant. It also mutates `refreshTokenResponse.data` when `success === false`, which will throw since `data` is undefined (though the preceding throw usually prevents this).

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys and validates nothing useful

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the string `"[object Object]"` for both entries (a ZodString stringifies to `[object Object]`), so the object literal collapses to a single property named `"[object Object]"` of type number/unknown. The comment claims 'any property with a number is the expiry' but Zod cannot express that this way. Effectively the credential-sharing path only validates `access_token` presence and silently accepts responses with no expiry, so expired tokens will be stored and reused.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key is overwritten with the Zod safeParse wrapper object

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. an object of the form `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. Here the return value is assigned to `key` and written straight into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The stored credential therefore becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` instead of the Google token object, so `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail on the next use and the user's Google Calendar integration breaks permanently until re-installed. The value must be `...data` (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`).

That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled, but several callers expect the shape produced by their own refresh function: zoho-bigin and zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data.*` (axios response), hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object with `expiresIn`/`accessToken`. With syncing enabled these will read `undefined` and store broken credentials (or throw). The sync branch needs per-app normalisation or each caller must handle both shapes.

With syncing enabled these will read `undefined` and store broken credentials (or throw). The sync branch needs per-app normalisation or each caller must handle both shapes.

`refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the third argument, which the helper treats as the Cal.com user id and forwards as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. This will request tokens for the wrong user (or a non-existent one). `refreshAccessToken` must receive and forward `credential.userId`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

Salesforce refresh result is discarded; stale access token still used

A refresh_token grant is now executed on every `getClient()` call (every service instantiation, even when the existing token is still valid — an unnecessary API round trip and rate-limit risk), but the returned connection is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old credential rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

`handler` accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without try/catch. Malformed bodies, a wrong encryption key, or a non-JSON plaintext throw and produce an unhandled 500 with a stack trace rather than a 400. Validate the method and return structured 400s.

This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean

The expression `process.env.A && process.env.B` yields `undefined`/`""`/the second string rather than a boolean, so the exported constant's type is `string | undefined`. Consumers use it in boolean contexts today, but the name implies a boolean and it would serialize oddly if ever returned from an API. Wrap in `!!`.

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret / signature header (the PR introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` but does not use it here), so anyone who can reach the self-hoster's endpoint can request tokens for an arbitrary user id. There is also no `Content-Type` header for the URL-encoded body and no `response.ok` check, so error pages are passed downstream as if they were token responses.

Diagnostic logging for failed Outlook token refresh removed

The previous code logged the Zod error and the raw Microsoft response when the refresh token response did not parse. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` with no detail, making Outlook refresh failures much harder to diagnose in production.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality and no empty-secret guard

The shared secret check uses `!==` on the header value, which is vulnerable to timing analysis; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Additionally, if the header is absent `req.headers[...]` is `undefined`; this is only safe because `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` requires the secret to be set, but that constant is a truthy string expression rather than a boolean, so any future refactor could allow `undefined === undefined` to pass.

Wrong app slug "zoomvideo" sent to credential sync endpoint

The Zoom app slug in the app store / credential records is `zoom` (see `createOAuthAppCredential({ appId: "zoom", ... })` in zoomvideo/api/callback.ts), but the refresh call passes `"zoomvideo"`. `prisma` used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
